subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm deciding to keep the vehicle model static without joints to minimize risk, rather than adding a root joint and turret rig, since static parts without joints should satisfy the requirements.

Now I'm sketching the design: a cyberpunk riot interceptor, a wide armored six-wheel truck with a roof-mounted water cannon turret, neon light bars, corporate logo decals, shield grilles, and side skirts, sized roughly 5.6m long, 2.4m wide, 2.6m tall. I'm planning to build it mostly from boxes and extruded/lathed shapes using the builder's part functions, with custom SVG textures for logos, hazard stripes, warning text, and an LED matrix display, plus hand-written paint functions instead of a prebuilt kit. I'm working out wheel placement and axle height, then starting to define the body's side-profile extrusion.

Still writing extrusion profile...

Total height roughly 2.9 with a roof light bar. For the paint, I'm planning a dark gunmetal navy body with panel lines and noise-based wear, darker toward the bottom, plus light accent trim.

For the overall palette I'm leaning cyberpunk: matte dark body with yellow-orange hazard stripes rather than full neon. Windows will be dark teal glass boxes, and I'm working out the windshield as a rotated thin box to create the sloped cabin front, calculating the slope angle from the geometry.

That rotation checks out, giving the windshield the right slope with a slight offset outward. Now I'm working out the side windows as thin glass-colored boxes positioned along the cabin's sloped sides, figuring out the right z and y ranges so they sit flush against the cabin geometry.

Next I'm designing the water cannon turret on the roof—base, turret box, and a forward-pointing barrel with a glowing frustum nozzle—plus considering side water tanks with level-indicator glow stripes and connecting hoses, and planning a front roof light bar with alternating cyan/magenta/blue neon segments.

I'm also adding underglow strips, bumper light accents, glowing headlight slits, a red tail bar, and neon side stripes, then designing a hazard-striped front push bumper as a textured box, and sketching a fictional "NOVA·SEC" security corp logo to place on the doors.

Working out the logo plane placement and orientation on each side so the text reads correctly when viewed from outside the vehicle, accounting for the mirrored geometry on the left versus right doors.

Now I'm positioning six wheels across three axles along the hull length, sizing tires and rims with a glowing cyan ring accent, and planning fender arches to cover the wheel-hull intersection.

Settling on 2.85 overall width, I'm now adding details: roof rack with antennas, sensor domes, camera pods, loudspeaker horns, A-pillar spotlights, a front ram grille with vertical bars, window mesh, side steps, exhaust stacks, and smoke grenade launcher tubes on the cabin sides. I'm also planning texture labels like LOGO, HAZARD, and LEDBOARD for the various panels.

I'm sketching out box-building helper functions for constructing parts without joints, keeping models static, and deciding how base paint colors and texture patterns will be applied across the body.

Writing the body paint function...

Still shaping the hull outline...

Designing the water cannon turret above the roof—base, rotating body, and an elevated barrel sweeping from the roof toward the front, clear of the windshield, with a flared nozzle tip.

Now I'm planning glowing cyan ring bands along the barrel for visual detail, then working out hose connections from a water tank to the turret, considering where to mount the tank—likely a cylindrical tank placed behind the turret on the rear roof area.

Barrel runs from z -1.0 to 1.0 with a nozzle extending further, positioned high enough to clear the lightbar. For the wheels I'm setting up a helper that builds a tire cylinder with dark paint, a steel hub, a glowing torus ring offset on the outer face, and a hub cap.

Now I'm adding mudguards as thin boxes over each wheel, with underglow strips along the sides for ground clearance lighting, and designing a front push-bar bumper with vertical bars and headlight slits built into the fascia.

Working out headlight placement and rotation to match the sloped front face geometry...

Now I'm thinking about adding a glowing cyan light strip across the bumper edge, then placing side logo decals on the hull, checking they clear the wheel wells.

I need to check fender clearance above the wheel tops to fit text without overlap — lowering fender height to y 1.16 and placing the text strip at y 1.35 should clear it, positioned at z around -0.92 between the wheels.

For the rear design, I'm planning a glowing LED board on the back face with neon "STAND DOWN" text, red tail light bars, hazard details on the rear doors, and twin bronze exhaust stacks mounted vertically at the rear corners.

Now I'm adding roof details: a camera turret sphere with a red glow lens, antenna rods, paired forward-facing loudspeaker horns, small glowing spotlights near the windshield pillars, and clustered tube-style grenade launchers mounted on the cabin sides.

I'm placing side mirrors with arm-and-box geometry, adding side step boxes positioned between the wheel wells, and sketching in thin door seam lines and skirt tabs for detail. For the logo texture, I'm designing a stylized "NOVAGUARD" emblem combining a circle and triangle motif on a transparent background.

Now I'm working through the remaining textures: hazard stripe patterns, an LED display reading "STAND DOWN" with a glowing dot grid, side unit text with yellow-on-black outline styling, a glass gradient with streak highlights, flat-colored lightbar glow boxes instead of gradients, and a tank texture with blue coloring and level stripe markings.

I'm tallying up seven total texture types (logo, hazard, LED, side text, glass, tank, plate) and planning a small "RC-2077" license plate detail on the bumper, plus scattering a few rivet rows along the hull roof using randomized positions for visual detail.

I'm defining small helper functions for building box and cylinder parts, and settling on part option conventions like default axis direction and flat-shading toggles.

Now I'm planning out specific positions—mirroring left/right sides, placing the three wheels along the z-axis, and figuring out the neon underglow strips along the hull bottom between the wheel gaps.

Skipping wipers, I'm adding roof corner strobe pods with red/blue glow and antenna rods, then working out the light bar housing position relative to the sloped roof and windshield geometry, placing small segmented boxes across its front face.

Writing the segment colors...

I'm finalizing the hull-cabin connection and skipping unused paint/extrude logic, aiming to keep the final code at a moderate length before writing it out in full.
